verdict.rationale: Reader's own docs show it converts URLs into LLM-friendly output. That output is markdown: `x-respond-with` can return "Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block", `x-markdown-chunking` operates on "the markdown response", and images are emitted in markdown image syntax. The docs also position this as "clean, LLM-ready text" in place of raw scraping output. Missing for 10: an explicit listing of the plain-markdown format option or default (only the frontmatter variant is shown verbatim), and independent hands-on confirmation of markdown output quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can receive scraped content as clean markdown instead of raw HTML

citations.quote: `frontmatter` returns **Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block**
`x-markdown-chunking` — opt-in semantic chunking of the markdown response.
The Reader API provides a streamlined, reliable output of clean, LLM-ready text.
It converts any URL to an **LLM-friendly** input with `https://r.jina.ai/https://your.url`.
